# Vendored third-party code

Both files are served straight from `web/vendor/` and cached by the service worker, so Play works
offline after the first load. Nothing here is generated by our tools; do not edit it by hand.

## stockfish.wasm.js + stockfish.wasm

- Upstream: `stockfish.js` 10.0.2 — https://github.com/niklasf/stockfish.js
- Engine: Stockfish, T. Romstad, M. Costalba, J. Kiiski, G. Linscott and contributors,
  with multi-variant support by Daniel Dugovic; compiled to WebAssembly by Niklas Fiekas.
- Licence: **GNU General Public License v3** — full text in `stockfish-COPYING.txt`.
- Why this build: it is single-threaded and touches no `SharedArrayBuffer`, so it runs on GitHub
  Pages, which sends no COOP/COEP headers. 655 KB for the pair. The 1.6 MB asm.js fallback that
  ships in the same package is deliberately NOT vendored; a browser without WebAssembly gets the
  "Glitch is asleep" path in `web/engine.js` instead.
- `stockfish.wasm.js` is itself the Web Worker script: `new Worker("vendor/stockfish.wasm.js")`.
  It loads `stockfish.wasm` from its own directory, so the two must stay side by side.

## chess.js

- Upstream: `chess.js` 1.0.0-beta.8 — https://github.com/jhlywa/chess.js
- Copyright (c) 2023 Jeff Hlywa. Licence: **BSD 2-Clause** — full text in `chess.js-LICENSE.txt`.
- The published build is CommonJS/ESM only. `chess.js` here is that build, unmodified between the
  two `chess.js begins/ends` markers, inside a wrapper that gives a plain `<script>` tag a
  `window.Chess` and still answers `require()` in the Node test suites. The trailing
  `sourceMappingURL` comment is stripped because the `.map` is not vendored.
